Aside: what's the cleanest way to handle missing quarters in a Vega-Lite line chart? Right now I think it just connects across them.
transcript.assistant:
By default Vega-Lite will connect line points across missing time buckets if there are simply no input rows for that bucket. You have three common ways to handle missing quarters, depending on whether you want gaps or interpolation:

- Insert explicit null points for the missing quarters so the line breaks there. You can generate a complete sequence of quarter keys (via a sequence/lookup or by constructing a table of quarters) and then join or impute so each missing quarter has a row with temperature = null. Vega-Lite will break the line at nulls, producing visible gaps.

- Use the impute transform to synthesize the missing quarters. impute can generate rows for missing keys; use method = "value" with value = null to produce gaps, or use method = "linear" (or other methods) to fill values by interpolation if you want a smoothed/filled line instead of gaps.

- Control drawing with the mark.defined property so the renderer only draws segments for defined values (useful when you already have explicit nulls or a computed flag). This is an alternative to inserting nulls, but you still need rows for the missing quarters if you want gaps to appear on a regular time axis.

Recommended: generate a complete sequence of quarters for your chart domain, then impute temperature to null for missing quarters if you want gaps, or impute with method:"linear" to interpolate. This preserves consistent spacing on the x-axis while letting you choose gap vs. interpolation.

transcript.user: Another aside - can Vega-Lite read a TSV directly, or do I need to convert to CSV first?
transcript.assistant:
Yes — Vega-Lite can load TSV directly. Use the data.url property with either the .tsv file extension (which is often auto-detected) or explicitly set a format, e.g. format: { "type": "tsv" }.

If you need explicit parsing (e.g., parse a date column or coerce numeric fields), you can also add a parse object (format.parse) or use Vega-Lite’s parsing via the encoding types / a parse transform. Also remember remote TSV files require appropriate CORS headers.
